case_study_insert.main_stem: Aldermont Route Optimisation (ARO) is a private limited company in the logistics technology (SaaS) sector, employing a workforce of 52. Founded in 2016 by Helena Duarte, the business supplies route-optimization software to national freight and delivery fleets and operates a flat organisational structure with democratic leadership. ARO plans to invest $1,000,000 in a new live-traffic AI route-optimization engine, financed by $700,000 of venture capital and $300,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $630,000 a year, a variable cost of $140 a unit and a selling price of $210, and currently produces 20,000 units a year. ARO faces two operational problems: customer onboarding is taking 6 weeks instead of the 4-week target, and labour turnover among customer-support staff has reached 17%.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations Log — Q3 2025: ARO's platform planned 18,400 routes last quarter across 240 fleet clients, with 96% of routes generated in under 3 minutes. Average client fuel use fell 11.5% and delivery miles per route fell 17%. Onboarding averages 6 weeks against a 4-week target. Customer complaints fell from 29 to 15 per month, but labour turnover in the support team reached 17%. Market research of 500 fleet managers found 68% would switch providers for a 15% fuel-saving guarantee, and 44% cite real-time traffic as their top priority. A training needs analysis shows 16 of 52 staff have not completed on-the-job training on the new engine; off-the-job courses at the logistics institute cost $800 per employee. Staff complete on-the-job training on the optimization engine and off-the-job training at the logistics institute.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Aldermont Route Optimisation for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank raised the base interest rate from 5.1% to 5.9%, lifting costs for variable-rate business loans. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 6.1% from $12.90 to $13.69 per hour from April 2026. (3) Diesel prices have risen 14.2% year-on-year and freight demand grew 5.5%, while transport and logistics inflation is running at 6.8% — making fuel efficiency a top buying criterion for fleets.

questions.question_text: ARO plans to raise $700,000 of the $1,000,000 expansion through venture capital. Explain two advantages for ARO of venture capital rather than a bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Venture capital carries no fixed repayment schedule and no monthly interest, so ARO avoids straining cash flow while fixed costs are already $630,000 a year. The live-traffic AI engine will take months to generate new subscription revenue from the 68% of 500 surveyed fleet managers willing to switch for a fuel-saving guarantee; equity financing lets ARO fund that ramp-up without breaching covenants or repossession risk on the platform.

Point 2: Venture capitalists typically bring logistics-sector expertise, introductions to national fleets and board credibility that accelerate enterprise sales — worth far more than cash to a 52-person private limited company competing against larger incumbents. Unlike a bank, a venture investor shares the downside if the engine launch slips beyond the 4-week onboarding target recovery, and Helena Duarte keeps control of daily operations while gaining a partner motivated to see the $1,000,000 investment succeed.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to Aldermont Route Optimisation and its expansion decision.

questions.question_text: ARO is launching its live-traffic AI route-optimization engine to national freight and delivery fleets. Consider a weekly webinar and demo series with live traffic simulations, advertising in Fleet Management Weekly trade magazine, or sponsoring a national logistics conference. Which should ARO choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Webinar and demo series with live traffic simulations: A weekly webinar lets ARO prove its strongest asset — 96% of 18,400 routes generated in under 3 minutes, delivering 11.5% average fuel savings — in front of exactly the 68% of the 500 surveyed fleet managers willing to switch for a 15% fuel-saving guarantee. Demonstrations are interactive, capture leads automatically, and cost little compared with a conference stand. Drawbacks are that some senior managers avoid webinars and attendance can fade after the first sessions, so ARO must keep content sharp and follow up personally within 48 hours.

Fleet Management Weekly advertising: A trade-magazine campaign reaches a targeted logistics readership and builds brand credibility cheaply over several months. However, print advertising is passive and hard to measure; fleet managers rarely switch SaaS providers on the strength of an advert, and the 11.5% fuel-saving proof is far more persuasive shown live than described on paper.

National logistics conference sponsorship: Sponsoring a headline national conference puts ARO in front of hundreds of fleet decision-makers and anchors its brand beside industry leaders. The cost is high for a 52-person business already carrying a $1,000,000 build, attendance includes non-buyers, and a one-off event generates leads unevenly rather than a dependable weekly pipeline.

Recommendation: ARO should choose the webinar and demo series. It is the only option that demonstrates live performance to the 68% of switch-ready fleet managers at low cost, generates measurable weekly leads, and lets ARO quantify 11.5% fuel savings in front of each prospect. The magazine advert is rejected as too passive to convert, and the conference sponsorship is rejected as a single, expensive burst of exposure unsuited to a long enterprise sales cycle and an expansion already absorbing venture capital.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited knowledge or outline of the promotional options with minimal context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of ARO with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options in the context of ARO with a well-justified recommendation explaining why the trade-magazine advert and conference sponsorship are rejected.

questions.question_text: ARO's labour turnover among customer-support staff has reached 17%. Explain two benefits for ARO of its democratic leadership style for its support and routes teams.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership lets support staff contribute ideas on ticket triage, onboarding checklists and route-engine quirks, which directly attacks the 6-week onboarding gap against the 4-week target. Staff who help design the onboarding flow flag real customer pain points the (small) management team cannot see, accelerating fixes and raising customer satisfaction while complaints have already fallen from 29 to 15 per month.

Point 2: Involving support and routes staff in decisions satisfies their esteem needs (Maslow) and builds ownership, which is critical when 17% labour turnover threatens service quality for 240 fleet clients. Higher retention saves replacement and retraining costs, protects the 11.5% fuel-saving commitments clients expect, and makes ARO's flat structure genuinely agile — democratic participation keeps the whole 52-person workforce aligned behind the $1,000,000 engine launch without adding expensive management layers.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to ARO's leadership style, support team and onboarding problem.

questions.question_text: ARO must train 16 support staff on the new live-traffic AI engine. Consider on-the-job training or off-the-job training at the logistics institute. Which should ARO choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Training during live support shifts costs nothing in fees, keeps the 16 staff available to answer 240 fleet clients, and lets them learn the new engine against real tickets — directly relevant to reducing response times and the 6-week onboarding gap. Senior staff or engineers can coach, and learning is reinforced daily. Drawbacks are that senior staff are pulled off their own queues at a time when labour turnover is 17% and support is stretched, training quality varies with the coach, and no external certificate is issued for enterprise clients' compliance teams.

Off-the-job training at the logistics institute: The institute course at $800 per employee delivers structured, up-to-date AI and route-optimisation instruction, costing $12,800 in total — affordable against the $1,000,000 expansion and revenue of $8,400,000. It lifts all 16 staff to the same standard, produces certificates clients respect, and removes the burden from senior engineers. The drawbacks are time away from the support desk during a demanding rollout and content that may not match ARO's proprietary engine exactly, so some shadowing would still be needed afterwards.

Decision: ARO should choose off-the-job training at the logistics institute. The engine is a sophisticated AI product and the support team is already under-resourced at 17% turnover; certified, structured training standardises skills, earns client confidence and avoids overloading senior staff. On-the-job training is rejected as the primary route because informal shadowing would deepen inconsistency and keep onboarding stuck at 6 weeks; ARO can pair each graduate with a senior engineer for one week afterwards to apply the course to live routes.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to ARO.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of one or both training methods in the context of ARO.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both training methods in the context of ARO with a well-justified decision covering cost, standardisation and support-capacity risk.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how ARO's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $630,000 ÷ ($210 − $140) = $630,000 ÷ $70 = 9,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 9,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $210 − $140 = $70. Answer: contribution per unit is $70.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways ARO's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Managers can compare the 9,000-unit break-even output with actual output of 20,000 units to confirm a margin of safety of 11,000 units, giving headroom to discount for the 68% of 500 fleet managers willing to switch providers for a fuel-saving guarantee.
2. Contribution per unit of $70 lets managers model a 5% price increase ahead of the live-traffic AI launch, testing whether the 15% fuel-saving proof point supports higher licence fees without losing the 44% of managers who prioritise real-time traffic.
3. Fixed costs of $630,000 a year and the $70 contribution help managers plan for the $700,000 venture capital: each new client covering the variable cost of $140 moves ARO toward covering fixed costs, so the investor can see a clear path from 20,000 to profitable scale.
4. Unit-cost data ($630,000 ÷ 20,000 units + $140 = $171.50 a unit) lets managers benchmark delivery cost per licence, target the cloud-hosting share of the $140 variable cost, and improve the support team's labour productivity of 385 units per staff member to bring onboarding back to the 4-week target.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 9,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $70 | (iii) Four contextual uses: the 11,000-unit margin of safety against 20,000 units supports switch-target discounting; contribution per unit of $70 tests price increases for the AI engine; fixed costs of $630,000 are mapped against the $700,000 venture capital; and unit costs of $171.50 benchmark cloud spend and the 4-week onboarding recovery.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate ARO's financial performance by calculating the gross profit margin, the profit margin and ROCE for 2024 and 2025. Has ARO's financial performance improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 40.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 44.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 12.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 14.0%
ROCE 2024 = 15.0%
ROCE 2025 = 17.5%

Detailed workings: Revenue climbed from $7,250,000 in 2024 to $8,400,000 in 2025, growth of 15.9%. Cost of sales rose from $4,350,000 to $4,704,000, a slower 8.1%, so gross profit improved from $2,900,000 to $3,696,000. Operating profit rose from $870,000 to $1,176,000, up 35.2% — more than double the revenue growth rate — showing operating leverage as fixed costs at $630,000 a year were spread over more licences. Capital employed rose from $5,800,000 to $6,720,000, up 15.9%, exactly matching revenue growth, and interest payable rose from $96,000 to $120,000 on increased borrowing.

Evaluation: Profitability improved on every measure. The gross improvement from 40.0% to 44.0% reflects better pricing power or cheaper delivery on the route-optimization engine, and complaints falling from 29 to 15 per month supports retention. The operating improvement from 12.0% to 14.0% shows ARO converting growth into profit despite the 6-week onboarding gap and 17% support turnover. The return on capital employed rose from 15.0% to 17.5%, confirming the platform is generating more from each dollar invested, though venture-capital dilution of equity means future returns must outrun investor expectations. Residual concerns: diesel-driven client hesitation, cloud-hosting inflation, and execution risk on the new live-traffic engine.

Conclusion: ARO's financial performance has improved. Revenue grew 15.9%, operating profit grew 35.2%, and both the conversion of revenue to profit and the return on capital employed moved upward for the second year. ARO must now keep onboarding at 4 weeks and the support team stable to compound these gains after the engine launch.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for both 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of revenue growth, cost leverage, capital employed and interest, and a justified conclusion on whether ARO's financial performance improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for ARO of adding an electric-vehicle routing and charging-stop planning module to its engine.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: An EV module would let ARO win fleets switching to electric vehicles as diesel prices rise 14.2% year-on-year — precisely the clients its research shows are ready to switch. With 68% of 500 fleet managers willing to switch providers, an EV-capable engine differentiates ARO from legacy rivals, opens a new premium-priced tier, and strengthens the fuel-efficiency story behind the $1,000,000 live-traffic AI launch, supporting higher contribution per unit than the current $70.

Disadvantage: Building EV routing requires accurate charging-station data, battery-range modelling and regulatory map licensing, diverting engineering capacity from the core AI engine already absorbing the $700,000 venture capital. Licence costs and messy real-world charging data could produce wrong recommendations, undermining the 96% of routes generated in under 3 minutes and the 11.5% fuel savings that anchor ARO's marketing — risking new quality complaints on top of the existing 6-week onboarding and 17% support turnover problems.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to ARO's engine, research data and expansion.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise from 5.1% to 5.9%, the 6.1% minimum wage increase and the 14.2% rise in diesel prices will affect ARO. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (5.1% to 5.9%): ARO is financed by $700,000 of venture capital and $300,000 of retained profit rather than a new bank loan, so the direct effect on the expansion is limited; existing interest payable of $120,000 could edge higher if any legacy debt is variable-rate. Higher rates may also slow fleets' willingness to invest in new vehicles and software, lengthening enterprise sales cycles. An indirect but real effect.

Diesel price rise (14.2% year-on-year): For ARO's clients this is a powerful demand driver — every 14.2% rise makes route-optimization with fuel savings more urgent. With 68% of 500 surveyed fleet managers willing to switch for a 15% fuel-saving guarantee and freight demand growing 5.5%, diesel inflation strengthens ARO's sales case, supports premium pricing on the live-traffic AI engine and should raise retention among 240 fleet clients. The risk is that struggling clients delay software purchases to fund fuel bills in the short term.

Minimum wage increase (6.1%, from $12.90 to $13.69 per hour): With 52 staff weighted toward customer-support and onboarding roles near the minimum wage, roughly 30 staff in such roles cost about 30 × 2,000 hours × $12.90 = $774,000 a year, so the 6.1% rise adds roughly $47,200 annually. Against operating profit of $1,176,000 that is a direct 4% hit, compounding the 17% support labour turnover problem and pushing ARO toward automation of triage or further price rises.

Conclusion: The 6.1% minimum wage increase will have the greatest impact on ARO's own finances — roughly $47,200 a year of unavoidable cost landing on exactly the support team already stretched by 17% turnover and 6-week onboarding. The diesel rise is strategically the most significant opportunity, expanding demand and strengthening ARO's value proposition, but it does not hit ARO's own cost base. The interest-rate rise is the smallest, largely neutralised by venture-capital funding. ARO should counter the wage pressure with support automation and improved onboarding to lift labour productivity above 385 units per employee.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to ARO.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on ARO's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes in the context of ARO with a well-justified judgement that the minimum wage increase has the greatest direct impact and why the other two differ.
